tasks.task: Write a wholesale pitch email to shops and distributors

items.when: Before writing, to plan how to reach this retailer's buyer and what keeps the shelf
When the pitch must carry the terms and line sheet a shop needs to say yes
When you need the first email, the follow-ups and a sending setup
When the opener reads like a pitch, to try one a busy shop owner would answer
When the email is written and needs subject lines from several angles
When samples would help, to set who gets one, how to claim it and what it costs
Before sending, to test each claim, check the legal basics and tighten the email

tasks.task: Write a line sheet a busy buyer can read in a minute

items.when: When products, wholesale prices, pack sizes and lead times must fit one clear sheet
Before listing prices, to check which products earn enough to offer at wholesale
When each product needs one true fact a shop can repeat to its customers
Before the sheet is sent, to catch wording that tells shops what they must charge
Before the sheet goes out, to check each item is in stock at the price on the order page

tasks.task: Write a plain wholesale terms summary

items.when: When minimum order, payment, shipping, returns and lead times must fit one page
Before setting prices, to know the true cost per sellable unit
When terms are drafted, to check margin per unit after the retailer's cut and freight
When volume breaks and exceptions need a matrix and approval limits
Before it is sent, to read the page as a shop owner and list what they would still ask

tasks.task: Group buyers and send reorder messages

items.when: When order history must be grouped into new, active, slowing and lapsed buyers
When you know how long stock lasts and need reorder messages with timing
When you want the emails split by buyer type and a read of results afterwards
When reorder emails go unopened, to try subject lines from several angles
Each month, to score repeat health from the order export and name one stage to fix

tasks.task: Design a referral or reseller partner programme

items.when: When the client wants to start or rebuild a referral, reseller or distributor programme
When partner types, the deal for each and the rules must come from the real margin
Before the design, to set out partner types, incentives and how shared revenue is tested
When the programme is referral or affiliate and needs rewards, a flow and a launch plan
When referral and reseller are both possible, to see each with money and dates
Before terms are fixed, to see what the partner keeps at forecast and at weaker sales
When the reward pays for sign-ups and the business needs customers who stay

tasks.task: Write a pitch to recruit partners

items.when: When the deal is worked out and one type of partner needs an invitation
When you are unsure which partners to invite, to get several ideas with a pitch for each
When you have never met them, to try an opener built on what they gain
Before sending, to test every earnings claim and tighten the email
When the pitch lists your benefits and gives the partner no proof others have earned

tasks.task: Write a stockist welcome pack

items.when: When a shop has placed its first order and should sell through and reorder
When the first 30 days need steps, milestones and who contacts the shop when
When shops keep asking the same things, to turn real questions into the pack's FAQ
Before the pack goes out, to check any line about shelf prices or promotions
When the pack is drafted, to read it as shop staff who have never seen the product

tasks.task: Write the partner programme launch pack

items.when: When the programme is approved and needs the announcement, how-to-join page and FAQ
When the launch is shared with a partner and each audience needs its own draft
When the FAQ must answer the awkward questions partners and staff will ask
When the launch needs timing and channels as well as the copy
Before the page goes live, to check the programme rules do not fix resale prices

tasks.task: Onboard partners and score their performance

items.when: When new partners need a first-30-day plan and the programme needs a fair scorecard
When partners must sell against a rival and need comparisons and reply scripts
When partners need a one-pager, an objection sheet or a demo script to use
When the scorecard is drafted, to see what it rewards and where it pulls the wrong way

tasks.task: Win back lapsed wholesale buyers

items.when: When you must find who has gone quiet by each buyer's own gap between orders
When you know the order gaps and the discount room and need the messages
When the whole order history needs sorting into who to win back and who to drop
Before a win-back offer goes out, to check the deepest discount the margin allows

tasks.task: Write account plans for the biggest buyers

items.when: When a key buyer needs a plan from its order history and what it has not yet stocked
When the plan needs goals, key people, risks and next steps written out
Before a review meeting, to get a health read, value delivered and an agenda
When one buyer is a large share of sales, to set limits and a plan if they leave

tasks.task: Write a one-page partner deal summary for the lawyer

items.when: When the commercial deal is agreed and must be written plainly for a lawyer
When the deal is not yet settled and needs the partner's profit sum and fair terms
When you have the offer and the partner's numbers and need a one-page term sheet
When the partner sends their own contract, to flag risky terms before the lawyer

tasks.task: Settle a deal registration conflict

items.when: When two partners, or a partner and your own team, claim the same customer
When the rules do not settle it, to look for a split both sides can accept
When one side must be told no, to say it with the real reason and keep the trust

tasks.task: Check wording that touches resale prices

items.when: Before any line sheet, terms page, partner email or fund rule is sent
When a whole partner marketing plan needs reading for rules it may break
When one line is in doubt, to get fine, needs a look or hold with a reason

tasks.task: Run the monthly channel review

items.when: In the first week of each month, for reorders, partner activity and payouts
When each partner's sales and active status must be scored against the programme rules
When the same channel numbers must be pulled and reported each month
Each quarter, to mark each partner type or programme keep, cut or double down

tasks.task: Decide which channels and partner types to use

items.when: When the choice of partner type depends on the margin each one leaves
When you have direct and partner sales costs and need cost to serve and return by channel
When the client wonders if selling direct would beat wholesale on their margins

tasks.task: Build a list of shops and distributors to approach

items.when: When you can describe the ideal stockist and need accounts with a reason for each
When the list needs buyer names and contact details added from many sources
When the list is long, to score fit and sort it into tiers to approach first

tasks.task: Prepare a pitch meeting with a retail buyer

items.when: When a retailer's buyer has agreed to meet and you need the case for the shelf
When the buyer needs a leave-behind with no made-up numbers
When the retailer holds the power, to set your terms and the order to move in
Before agreeing promotions or listing fees, to see the margin left per unit
When the pitch is about your brand and should be about what the shop sells per shelf
When the buyer asks for a deeper discount and you need calm questions, not a concession

tasks.task: Evaluate a partner or distributor who approached you

items.when: When a partner proposes a deal, to get a sign or pass call and terms to ask for
Before signing, to check the people for ability, energy and honesty
When their numbers look generous, to test what each side keeps if sales fall short

tasks.task: Plan a joint campaign with a partner

items.when: When a partner is on board and you need a joint plan and what each side does
When the campaign is a shared event and seats, follow-up and leads must be planned
When a marketing fund has rules, to check they do not tie support to resale prices

tasks.task: Plan a trade show and follow up the leads

items.when: Before booking, to plan the show as a test with costs, measures and decision rules
When stand staff need 10, 30 and 60 second answers and an opening question
After the show, to group buyers by what each asked for and draft the follow-ups

tasks.task: Forecast wholesale demand and allocate stock

items.when: When you have past wholesale orders and need a forecast and a way to track its error
When a new buy must be split across stockists by what each one sells

tasks.task: Chase overdue trade invoices

items.when: When several shops are late, to get a reminder for each, gentle or firm
When one account matters, to try a reminder that starts from your history with them
Before reminders go, to check the amounts and dates match the invoices

always.when: Before any terms, pitch or pack leaves, to tie each price and fact to the client's records
Before anything goes to a buyer or partner, to catch typos and one term used two ways

helpers.when: When wholesale, distributor and shelf prices must be set as one ladder from the margin
When the line sheet or welcome pack needs a designed layout for print or PDF
When wholesale orders outrun stock and lead times need planning
When trade credit, statements and late payers need a proper process
When the target is a large account that needs an account plan and a first visit
When programme rules or distributor terms raise competition or consumer law questions

gaps: No library item writes a line sheet or a wholesale terms summary; only the kit covers them
No library item writes a stockist welcome pack with display, staff notes and reorder steps
No library item finds stockists by region and shop type or covers wholesale marketplaces such as Faire
No library item sets deal registration rules or settles a registration conflict
No library item calculates partner commissions and payouts each month
No library item builds a partner scorecard or a partner's first-30-day plan
No library item checks resale price wording against competition law
No library item drafts distributor terms such as exclusivity, territory and minimum volumes
No library item builds partner training or a short certification
No library item offers different line sheet layouts or welcome pack versions to compare
No tool guide covers partner management or wholesale ordering platforms
No mind in the library is built on a channel or wholesale thinker
